links.outcome: Mental health professionals' perceptions of chatbot harm, dependence, and manipulation risk
links.effect: Professionals had emphatic initial impressions of responses likely to produce harm and a generic mode of care, and saw risk of user dependence and manipulation. Trust scores were medium to low, with no difference between chatbots (t6=-0.76; P=.48).
links.quote: Qualitative analysis revealed emphatic initial impressions among mental health professionals of chatbot responses likely to produce harm, exhibiting a generic mode of care, and risking user dependence and manipulation given the central role of trust in the therapeutic relationship.

screen.reason: Mixed methods evaluation by mental health professionals assessing the safety, clinical implications, and risks of two commercial mental health chatbots.
